newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese freed by Zaire rebels arrive in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese freed by Zaire rebels arrive in Beirut.

text.p: Lebanese nationals, released by Zairean rebels last week after being held nearly a month in the diamond capital of Mbuji-Mayi, arrived in Beirut.
The 24 men and two women who arrived late on Wednesday -- part of 43 who had been held in Zaire -- looked tired. All declined to be identified.
"We have only hand-luggage as you see, we left all our belongings and life-savings behind to save our souls," one returnee told Reuters.
Five of the remaining 17 Lebanese stayed in Zaire while the rest went to European capitals, another returnee said.
Zairean rebels confined the Lebanese, most of them diamond traders, to their homes in Mbuji-Mayi demanding payment of "back taxes".
The rebels initially demanded $750,000 but reportedly settled on $250,000. They released the Lebanese after mediation by the Lebanese and South African governments and OAU-UN envoy Mohamed Sahnoun.
Only a fifth of Lebanese nationals who were in Zaire have remained, a returnee said. There were 5,000 Lebanese registered in the Central African country, most of them traders.
